newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing's CEO to meet Van Miert on McDonnell deal.
newsitem.headline: Boeing's CEO to meet Van Miert on McDonnell deal.

text.p: Boeing Co President and CEO Phil Condit will meet European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert on Tuesday to discuss the alliance with McDonnell Douglas Corp.

The meeting comes only a week before the Commission will decide whether to clear the $13.3 billion alliance or, as it is widely expected, to start a full investigation due to fears it might harm fair competition in Europe.
Condit will see Van Miert at 1430 GMT after attending a lunchtime meeting organised by the European Aviation Club in Brussels, Commission and company sources said on Friday.

Boeing's chief will arrive in London on Monday for a week-long European tour, which company officials say was scheduled months before last December's surprise announcement of the proposed alliance with its rival civil and military aircraft maker.

"He is not lobbying. He wants to meet with some key industrialists," Belgian public relations firm PRP, which represents Boeing, told Reuters. Condit was meeting Van Miert "out of courtesy", PRP said.
Condit is also expected to travel to Germany and France before returning to the United States either Friday or Saturday. There was no information on who he will be meeting other than Van Miert.
The EU's competition chief warned only a few days after the alliance was announced that the Commission would have to assess whether the deal will strengthen Boeing's dominant position in Europe.

The deal was submitted to the EU for clearance on February 18. The Commission has until March 19 to approve it or start an in-depth probe, which could last up to four months, after having studied comments from rival aircraft manufacturers and airlines.

Boeing currently controls about 60 percent of the worldwide market for commercial jets. The alliance with McDonnell leaves the market with only one other competitor: the European Airbus Industrie consortium with a share of about 35 percent.
Airbus filed "detailed comments" on the alliance with the Commission this week, a company official told Reuters. He declined to elaborate.

A consortium source also said Airbus was to comment on behalf of its partners on the impact on the fixed-wing aircraft sector. Its partners would file separate views on the effect on helicopters and the defense and space industries.
Airbus comprises Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace, Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
